messages:
mia: Acme reports embeddings vectors/sec dropped ~3x starting 03:20 UTC, tokens/sec looks normal. request_id=acme-req-778
acme-sre: yep, hitting more 429s on /v1/embeddings, vectors/sec 120 -> 40, payload dims 1024 unchanged
omar: can you paste a minimal curl we can replay?
acme-sre: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-embed-1\",\"input\": [\"...text...\"]}'
elaine: any recent batching or routing rollout around 03:15-03:25?
jake: we shipped a batching policy change at 03:12 that reduced batch_window_ms 12 -> 6 for latency SLOs on gpu-pool-08 (canary then global)
mia: that change plus autoscaler behavior can cause many small batches for embeddings, increasing kernel call overhead and starving vectorization path. also check kv_cache lock timeouts
infra-bot: ALERT gpu-pool-08 queue_depth p95=84 @ 03:18 UTC, pods_waiting=12
omar: acme, can you share a short log snippet around the failed req id? specifically any 'kv_cache_lock' or 'batch-window' tags
acme-sre: attaching snippet: \"ERROR kv_cache_lock timeout on shard 3 req=acme-req-778\" and several \"enqueue wait >50ms\" lines
jake: repro steps for runtime team:
```
# replay sample traffic at 200 qps
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["short text"]}' &
done
wait
```
omar: quick hypothesis: reduced batch_window -> more tiny batches -> kernel overhead + increased scheduling -> GPU concurrency high but per-batch utilization low -> vectors/sec drops. tokens/sec unaffected because token path uses caching and autoreg batch coalescing differently
elaine: agree. also kv cache lock timeouts indicate coordination thrash when many small concurrent requests touch same embeddings shards
mia: action plan:
- revert batch_window_ms to 12 on gpu-pool-08 canary immediately (done 03:45)
- collect kernel wait stacks + GPU telemetry for 03:10-03:50
- run replay at canary to validate recovery
- add a regression test that measures vectors/sec vs batch_window_ms
- notify billing for potential mitigation window
jake: rolled back canary at 03:45 -> observing vectors/sec climb back to ~115 within 5m. infra metrics show queue_depth p95 down to 12 by 03:52
acme-sre: confirming our traffic recovered, saw 200 -> 110 vectors/sec then normal. thanks :tada:
omar: logs show kv_cache_lock errors drop after rollback, and kernel launch latency tail improved
elaine: root cause summary (for postmortem): batching policy rollback reduced batch_window too aggressively; combined with autoscaler instance churn this led to many small embedding batches, causing kernel overhead and KV cache lock contention -> vectors/sec regression while tokens/sec stayed constant.
mia: PR created for a safer rollout: gating batch_window shrink behind a throughput check + add canary size limit (#4123)
jake: will add an alert for vectors/sec deviation vs tokens/sec to catch similar regressions earlier
elaine: assigning postmortem owner @mia, tagging infra and runtime. also approving billing credit for impacted interval
acme-sre: appreciate the quick response and the rollback. will reach out if anything else pops up
mia: closing thread once postmortem is posted, leaving notes in incident tracker
_meta: generated by dataset-gen: embeddings throughput regression investigation, includes repro steps, logs, actions, rollback
